title: TCGA-BRCA lobular vs ductal: Phikon-v2 cells

about.summary: Each point is one 16 µm cell of a tissue tile from a breast cancer diagnostic slide, embedded by Phikon-v2 and projected with UMAP. Invasive lobular and invasive ductal carcinoma, balanced within hospitals: 40 patients from 10 hospitals, 240 tiles, 11,760 cells. The same tiles are shown for Virchow2 and Phikon-v2.

sections.title: Source
items: TCGA-BRCA diagnostic slides (H&E, formalin-fixed, one slide per patient), served by the Digital Slide Archive (api.digitalslidearchive.org); every tile is loaded from there when you hover.
Diagnosis from the NCI Genomic Data Commons (GDC), field primary_diagnosis.

sections.title: Case selection
items: Hospitals: the 10 TCGA tissue source sites with the most cases of both histotypes.
From each hospital, 2 cases with 'Lobular carcinoma, NOS' and 2 with 'Infiltrating duct carcinoma, NOS', drawn at random (seed 0); combined or other diagnoses are not used.

sections.title: Tile selection
items: Tissue is found on the slide thumbnail by colour (saturation above 0.07 and brightness above 0.2); tiles of 112 µm whose footprint is at least 95 % tissue are eligible.
6 eligible tiles per slide are drawn at random (seed 0) and read at 0.5 µm per pixel. No model output is used to choose tiles, so tiles may show tumour, stroma, fat or other tissue.

sections.title: Processing
items: Phikon-v2 (Owkin; ViT-L/16, self-supervised with the DINOv2 recipe on public pathology slides), applied to each tile at 224 × 224 px (0.5 µm per pixel).
Patch tokens of 8 µm after the final layer norm, averaged 2 × 2 into a 7 × 7 grid of 16 µm cells (one point per cell).
UMAP with cosine distance, 30 neighbours, min_dist 0.1, random_state 0.

sections.title: Colour options (ground truth only)
items: histotype: the patient's diagnosis in the pathology report (lobular or ductal). It describes the patient, not the cell: a lobular point may lie in stroma or fat.
hospital: TCGA tissue source site (characters 6-7 of the case id).

sections.title: Caveats
items: There are no tissue annotations for these slides, so it is unknown which cells show tumour.
40 patients, one slide each, 6 tiles per slide: a small sample for comparing histotypes.
UMAP distorts global distances; nearby points are similar, far-apart clusters are not necessarily dissimilar.
